acknowledge.text: You're rested. That's worth noticing.

options.title: Notice what helped
options.text: What helped you rest well? Sleep, a slower day, something else?
options.why: Knowing what helps you rest can make it easier to repeat.

options.title: Spend it well
options.text: Use some of this fresh energy on something that matters to you.
options.why: Rested energy can often go further than usual.

acknowledge.text: Calm. A good, quiet place to be.

options.title: Stay with it
options.text: Take a few slow breaths and just notice the calm.
options.why: Lingering in calm can help you find your way back to it later.

options.title: A note for a tense day
options.text: Write to yourself for a tense day: what does calm feel like?
options.why: A reminder from a calm moment can be easier to trust on a hard one.

acknowledge.text: Content. Things are enough right now.

options.title: Name what is enough
options.text: What, right now, is enough?
options.why: Noticing "enough" can help it stay a little longer.

options.title: Enjoy something simple
options.text: A drink, a view, a song. Enjoy it slowly.
options.why: Simple pleasures often feel richest when we slow down for them.

acknowledge.text: Relaxed. Let yourself stay here a while.

options.title: No rush
options.text: If you can, let the next thing wait a little.
options.why: Letting a relaxed moment last can be a good kind of rest.

options.title: A calm sound
options.text: Put on rain or waves in the background.
options.why: A gentle sound can help a relaxed feeling last.

acknowledge.text: You're in a thinking mood. A good time for a question.

options.title: Think on paper
options.text: What has been on your mind lately?
options.why: Thoughtful moods are often good for writing things through.
options.prompt: What's been on my mind lately:

options.title: One big question
options.text: What matters most to you this month?
options.why: A quiet, thoughtful mood can make big questions easier to look at.
options.prompt: What matters most to me this month:

acknowledge.text: You're quietly turning something over.

options.title: Let it out on the page
options.text: What are you thinking about?
options.why: Writing a thought out can help it settle.

options.title: A slow walk
options.text: A short, unhurried walk can give thoughts room.
options.why: Many people find walking helps thoughts unwind.

acknowledge.text: You did something, and it feels good.

options.title: Write it down
options.text: What did you do, and how did it feel?
options.why: Recording a win can help you remember it on harder days.
options.prompt: What I did, and how it felt:

options.title: Rest on it
options.text: Take a moment before rushing to the next thing.
options.why: Pausing after something done can let the satisfaction land.

acknowledge.text: What you are doing feels worth it. That matters.

options.title: Why it matters
options.text: What makes this worthwhile to you?
options.why: Knowing why something matters can help on days it feels hard.
options.prompt: Why this is worthwhile to me:

options.title: A letter for a doubting day
options.text: Write to yourself for a day when it does not feel worth it.
options.why: Your own reasons, in your own words, can help later.

acknowledge.text: You feel respected. A good feeling to notice.

options.title: Notice who and how
options.text: Who showed you respect, and how?
options.why: Noticing respect can help you recognise the people who are good for you.

options.title: Return it
options.text: Show someone else the same respect today.
options.why: Respect often grows when it is given back.

acknowledge.text: Someone appreciated you. You deserve it.

options.title: Keep the words
options.text: Write down what was said, for later.
options.why: Kind words, kept, can be read again on a hard day.

options.title: Pass it on
options.text: Tell someone else what you appreciate about them.
options.why: Appreciation tends to spread when it is shared.

acknowledge.text: You feel valued. You are.

options.title: What do you bring?
options.text: What do you bring to the people around you?
options.why: Naming your strengths can help you hold on to them.
options.prompt: What I bring to the people around me:

options.title: For a doubting day
options.text: Write to yourself for a day when you forget this.
options.why: Your own words can be a good reminder later.

acknowledge.text: You feel you can trust. That is a gift.

options.title: Let them know
options.text: Tell someone you trust that you appreciate them.
options.why: Trust often grows when it is spoken about.

options.title: What makes trust possible?
options.text: What helps you feel you can trust someone?
options.why: Knowing what builds trust can help in future relationships.

acknowledge.text: You're open and responsive. A good place to connect from.

options.title: Reach out
options.text: Ask someone how they really are.
options.why: Being open can help a conversation go deeper.

options.title: Listen inward too
options.text: What would you like, today?
options.why: Responsiveness can be turned towards yourself as well.

acknowledge.text: You feel steady in what you believe in.

options.title: Name it
options.text: What are you holding faith in right now?
options.why: Writing it down can make it a steady thing to return to.

options.title: For a wobbly day
options.text: Write to yourself for a day when this feels shaky.
options.why: Your own steadiness can be good company later.

acknowledge.text: Memories feel close today.

options.title: Write the memory
options.text: What are you remembering, and what does it mean to you?
options.why: Writing memories down can keep them warm.

options.title: Share it
options.text: Send someone from the memory a message.
options.why: Shared memories often bring people a little closer.

acknowledge.text: Thankful. A good feeling to stay with.

options.title: Three things
options.text: Write three things you are thankful for.
options.why: Writing down thanks can help you notice more good things.

options.title: Say thank you
options.text: Thank someone, today, for something specific.
options.why: A specific thank you often means a lot to the person who hears it.

acknowledge.text: You feel like looking after someone. Lovely.

options.title: Care for someone
options.text: Do one kind thing for someone you love.
options.why: Caring for others can be good for us too.

options.title: Include yourself
options.text: Do one kind thing for yourself as well.
options.why: The care you give others is something you deserve too.

acknowledge.text: You feel close to someone. A precious feeling.

options.title: Tell them
options.text: Let them know what they mean to you.
options.why: Saying it out loud can deepen closeness.

options.title: Keep the moment
options.text: Write a line about this closeness, for later.
options.why: Moments of closeness can be good to remember on lonelier days.

acknowledge.text: Love is in the room, or on your mind.

options.title: Show it
options.text: Do something small that shows your love.
options.why: Small acts of love often matter more than big ones.

options.title: Write to someone
options.text: Write a few lines to someone you love, even if you never send them.
options.why: Putting love into words can be a joy in itself.
options.prompt: A few lines to someone I love:

acknowledge.text: Serene. Everything feels still.

options.title: Breathe into it
options.text: A few slow breaths, nothing else.
options.why: Slow breathing can help a peaceful moment last.

options.title: Remember how it feels
options.text: Notice where this stillness sits in your body.
options.why: Knowing how serenity feels can help you find it again.
